SMTO-SKL-0160 — SMTO couldn't find that GitHub repository

GUID: 7325ddd2-3bc5-56a7-943f-7e0882759929
Slug: github-repository-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't tell which repository you meant, or GitHub said it isn't there. GitHub also says this when a private repository exists but your token isn't allowed to see it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the repository on github.com and copy its owner and name from the address, then repeat your request naming it as owner/name. SMTO only works with a repository it can identify exactly, and spelling must match GitHub's.
  2. On github.com, check that your token's repository access includes this repository. GitHub hides private repositories a token can't see, so it looks as if they don't exist.
  3. If the repository belongs to an organization, check that the organization has approved your token. Some organizations block tokens until an owner approves them.

What success looks like

  • When you ask SMTO about the repository, it shows its name and details.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume the repository was deleted; it may just be hidden from your token.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Repository resolution found no recognized github.com repository in the arguments, references or verified Git remotes, or a repository-scoped GitHub request returned HTTP 404.

What this means

  • Repository context resolves no recognized unique GitHub repository, or a repository-scoped API request receives HTTP 404. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Repository context resolves no recognized unique GitHub repository, or a repository-scoped API request receives HTTP 404.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish missing local repository evidence from a provider response that can hide a private repository.

How to fix it

  • resolve() found no github.com HTTPS/SSH remote in owner/repo, repository_ref or verified Git Working Context remotes, or the GET repository endpoint for owner/repo returned 404 (may_be_inaccessible=true). Supply the exact owner/repo, and check the PAT's selected repositories, permissions and organization/SSO approval before concluding the repository is absent.
  • Supply exact owner/repo or a recognized GitHub Git Repository reference. GitHub may hide a private repository as 404; verify selected repositories, token permissions and organization/SSO approval before concluding it is absent.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact authorized owner/repo resolves under the selected account.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
